- Bank linkage: banks' lending to nonbank financial institutions rose sharply after 2022 (est.). Research on this is linked to Fed and IMF work.
- Policy attention: the IMF Global Financial Stability Report (April 2024) had a chapter on private credit risks (est.). The BIS, ECB and Fed also published analyses (est.).
- Retail access: interval funds, non-traded BDCs and evergreen vehicles expanded (est.). Research here is thin.

## Method and limits
- Windows: research 2017 to 2025, so the gap to today (2026-10-23) is about 296 days from year-end 2025. News is 2019-01-01 to 2026-05-01, a gap of about 175 days. The new-work list covers publications from 2022 onward [c1].
- Lane: one call, research.radar. Index coverage was reported as complete by row floors, but the tool states this is not proof of ingest completeness [c1].
- Match mode: title-phrase matching on "private credit". It captures bank-credit-to-private-sector papers as well as direct-lending papers, so counts overstate the finance-industry sense. It also misses papers on "direct lending" or "non-bank lending" that do not use the phrase.
- Counts are typed papers and news items matching the phrase. They are not citations to the topic and not a measure of quality or market activity. The "new work" list is the most-cited papers, so recent papers are disadvantaged by citation lag.
- Censoring: only endpoints, peak and thirds were returned for the trends; year-by-year values were not. The final news month may be incomplete.
- Interpretation: the two-meanings split, the venue tiers, and "news grew faster than research" as a headline. Orientation labels reflect the paper's own framing, not the truth [c1].
- No figures from memory were used.
